phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ra.
phrases.explanation: The surah begins with the separated letters Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ra, whose full meaning is not explained here. They introduce verses of the Book and call the listener to attend to what follows.

phrases.translation: These are the verses of the Book. What has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe
phrases.explanation: What is revealed to the Prophet from his Lord is declared to be the truth. The statement affirms the source and reliability of the message. Most people do not believe. The verse acknowledges widespread rejection without suggesting that disbelief changes the truth of the revelation.

phrases.translation: It is Allah Who has raised the heavens without pillars—as you can see—then established Himself on the Throne. He has subjected the sun and the moon, each orbiting for an appointed term.
phrases.explanation: Allah raised the heavens without visible pillars, as people can observe. The verse directs attention to the order of the sky as a sign of the Creator’s power. Allah established the heavens and subjected the sun and moon, each moving for an appointed term. Their regular courses show an ordered creation under His authority.

phrases.translation: He conducts the whole affair. He makes the signs clear so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord
phrases.explanation: Allah conducts every affair. The verse connects the great motions of the heavens with His continuing governance of the world. Allah makes His signs clear so people may be certain of meeting their Lord. Reflection on creation is meant to strengthen awareness of the coming return and accountability.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who spread out the earth and placed firm mountains and rivers upon it, and created fruits of every kind in pairs.
phrases.explanation: Allah spreads out the earth and places mountains and rivers upon it. These features make the land a place where people can live and find water. Fruits of many kinds are created in pairs. Their variety and pattern invite attention to the provision and order built into the earth.

phrases.translation: He covers the day with night. Surely in this are signs for those who reflect
phrases.explanation: Allah covers the day with night. The recurring transition is a visible sign for those who reflect on the world around them. The earth’s features and cycles are signs for reflective people. The verse encourages observation that moves from natural patterns toward recognition of their Creator.

phrases.translation: And on the earth there are ˹different˺ neighbouring tracts, gardens of grapevines, ˹various˺ crops, palm trees—some stemming from the same root, others standing alone. They are all irrigated with the same water, yet We make some taste better than others. Surely in this are signs for those who understand
phrases.explanation: The earth contains neighbouring tracts, vineyards, crops, and palm trees, some sharing roots and others growing separately. The variety exists side by side in the same landscape. Although the plants receive the same water, their tastes differ. The contrast shows that identical basic conditions can produce distinct results by Allah’s design. These differences are signs for people who understand. The verse asks readers to consider the variety and provision around them rather than take it for granted.

phrases.translation: ˹Now,˺ if anything should amaze you ˹O Prophet˺, then it is their question: “When we are reduced to dust, will we really be raised as a new creation?”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers find resurrection astonishing and ask how people reduced to dust could be created again. The question expresses resistance to life beyond death, not a lack of Allah’s power.

phrases.translation: It is they who have disbelieved in their Lord. It is they who will have shackles around their necks. And it is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: The verse says they have disbelieved in their Lord and will have shackles around their necks. The image portrays the consequence of persistent rejection. They will be residents of the Fire forever. The warning sets their denial of resurrection beside the lasting accountability they refuse to accept.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ to hasten the torment rather than grace, though there have ˹already˺ been ˹many˺ torments before them. Surely your Lord is full of forgiveness for people, despite their wrongdoing, and your Lord is truly severe in punishment
phrases.explanation: The opponents ask for punishment to be hastened rather than for mercy, though earlier peoples already faced punishment. The verse reminds them that the warning has precedents. Allah is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing. The statement leaves room for repentance and does not treat punishment as the only possible response. Allah is also severe in punishment. Mercy should not be mistaken for permission to persist in wrongdoing or proof that accountability will never come.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “If only a sign could be sent down to him from his Lord.” You ˹O Prophet˺ are only a warner. And every people had a guide
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers demand a sign from the Prophet’s Lord. Their demand implies that the signs and guidance already given are not enough for them. The Prophet is a warner, and every people has a guide. His role is to convey warning, while guidance reaches communities through those appointed to show them the way.

phrases.translation: Allah knows what every female bears and what increases and decreases in the wombs. And with Him everything is determined with precision
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what every female carries and what increases or decreases in the womb. The verse affirms knowledge of development hidden from human observation. Everything with Allah is determined with precision. The detail of creation is not random or unknown to Him, even when people cannot see it.

phrases.translation: ˹He is the˺ Knower of the seen and the unseen—the All-Great, Most Exalted
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what is seen and unseen and is All-Great, Most Exalted. Nothing hidden escapes His knowledge, and nothing in creation rivals His greatness. His knowledge includes every concealed thought and every public act.

phrases.translation: It is the same ˹to Him˺ whether any of you speaks secretly or openly, whether one hides in the darkness of night or goes about in broad daylight
phrases.explanation: Secret and open speech are equally known to Allah, as are those who hide at night and those who walk in daylight. Changing the setting cannot conceal a person from divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: For each one there are successive angels before and behind, protecting them by Allah’s command. Indeed, Allah would never change a people’s state ˹of favour˺ until they change their own state ˹of faith˺.
phrases.explanation: Successive angels guard each person by Allah’s command. Their protection operates under His authority and does not make them independent of Him. Allah does not change a people’s favorable state until they change what is within themselves. The verse links communal change with people’s own choices and faith.

phrases.translation: And if it is Allah’s Will to torment a people, it can never be averted, nor can they find a protector other than Him
phrases.explanation: If Allah wills to torment a people, the decision cannot be stopped by human wishes. The warning reminds the audience that divine judgment is not controlled by worldly power. They will find no protector besides Allah. The verse calls people to seek His care rather than assume another power can shield them from His decree.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who shows you lightning, inspiring ˹you with˺ hope and fear, and produces heavy clouds
phrases.explanation: Allah shows people lightning that inspires both hope and fear. The flash can promise rain while also reminding people of nature’s power and their vulnerability. He produces heavy clouds. The clouds carry provision and are part of the signs through which people can reflect on Allah’s power and care.

phrases.translation: The thunder glorifies His praises, as do the angels in awe of Him. He sends thunderbolts, striking with them whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Thunder glorifies Allah, as do the angels in awe of Him. The verse presents even powerful natural forces as subject to their Creator. Allah sends thunderbolts and strikes whom He wills. The image underscores His power over events that people cannot command or predict.

phrases.translation: Yet they dispute about Allah. And He is tremendous in might
phrases.explanation: Despite these signs, people dispute about Allah. The contrast shows that witnessing power in creation does not automatically make everyone accept the truth. Allah is tremendous in might. The closing statement reinforces the scale of His power and the weakness of human opposition.

phrases.translation: Calling upon Him ˹alone˺ is the truth. But those ˹idols˺ the pagans invoke besides Him ˹can˺ never respond to them in any way. ˹It is˺ just like someone who stretches out their hands to water, ˹asking it˺ to reach their mouths, but it can never do so. The calls of the disbelievers are only in vain
phrases.explanation: Calling upon Allah alone is the true way. The verse directs worship toward the One who can hear and answer, rather than toward powerless substitutes. The idols cannot respond, like water that a person reaches toward but cannot bring to the mouth. The image conveys the futility of asking powerless objects for help. The calls of disbelievers are in vain. Their worship does not achieve the response they seek because the objects invoked have no power to answer them.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and the earth—willingly or unwillingly—as do their shadows, morning and evening
phrases.explanation: All in the heavens and earth bow to Allah, willingly or unwillingly. The verse describes universal submission to His authority, whether or not a person chooses conscious worship. Even their shadows bow morning and evening. The changing shadows reflect the created order and reinforce that everything remains subject to Allah.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” Say, “Allah!” Ask ˹them˺, “Why ˹then˺ have you taken besides Him lords who cannot even benefit or protect themselves?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet asks who is Lord of the heavens and earth, and the answer is Allah. The question begins by making the audience acknowledge the Creator’s authority. The Prophet asks why people worship lords that cannot benefit or protect themselves. The question challenges the logic of trusting powerless beings with matters of ultimate importance.

phrases.translation: Say, “Can the blind and the sighted be equal? Or can darkness and light be equal?” Or have they associated with Allah partners who ˹supposedly˺ produced a creation like His, leaving them confused between the two creations? Say, “Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Supreme.”
phrases.explanation: The comparison asks whether the blind and seeing, or darkness and light, are equal. It uses familiar contrasts to distinguish guidance from ignorance and truth from error. The verse asks whether Allah’s supposed partners created anything like His creation. The question challenges claims that would confuse the Creator with beings who have no comparable power. Allah is the Creator of all things, the One and the Supreme. The conclusion gathers the argument into a clear declaration of His unique authority.

phrases.translation: He sends down rain from the sky, causing the valleys to flow, each according to its capacity. The currents then carry along rising foam, similar to the slag produced from metal that people melt in the fire for ornaments or tools.
phrases.explanation: Rain fills valleys in proportion to their capacity. The image allows for different amounts while showing how water travels through the land and sustains life. The flowing water carries foam, as melted metal produces slag when people make ornaments or tools. The two examples prepare a comparison between what lasts and what is discarded.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah compares truth to falsehood. The ˹worthless˺ residue is then cast away, but what benefits people remains on the earth. This is how Allah sets forth parables
phrases.explanation: Allah uses the images of water and metal to compare truth with falsehood. Both processes separate useful substance from a temporary surface that may appear prominent. The worthless residue is cast away, while what benefits people remains on earth. The parable shows that falsehood may appear for a time, but lasting benefit belongs to truth. Allah sets forth these parables so people can understand. The images make an abstract contrast visible through ordinary experiences of rain, metal, and useful materials.

phrases.translation: Those who respond to ˹the call of˺ their Lord will have the finest reward. As for those who do not respond to Him, even if they were to possess everything in the world twice over, they would certainly offer it to ransom themselves. They will face strict judgment, and Hell will be their home. What an evil place to rest
phrases.explanation: Those who respond to their Lord receive the finest reward. The verse presents a willing answer to guidance as the path toward lasting good. Those who refuse would offer everything in the world twice over to escape the consequence. Wealth that seemed valuable in life cannot buy freedom at judgment. They face strict judgment, and Hell becomes their home. The warning contrasts their refusal with the reward of those who respond to Allah.

phrases.translation: Can the one who knows that your Lord’s revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ is the truth be like the one who is blind? None will be mindful ˹of this˺ except people of reason
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts someone who knows the revelation is true with someone who is blind to it. The difference is awareness of guidance, not physical sight. Only people of reason will be mindful of this distinction. Reflection helps them recognize the truth and act on what they know.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who honour Allah’s covenant, never breaking the pledge
phrases.explanation: The people of reason honor Allah’s covenant and do not break their pledges. Faithfulness to commitments is presented as a defining part of a thoughtful religious life. The covenant matters even when keeping it is inconvenient.

phrases.translation: and those who maintain whatever ˹ties˺ Allah has ordered to be maintained, stand in awe of their Lord, and fear strict judgment
phrases.explanation: They maintain the ties Allah has ordered to be maintained, stand in awe of Him, and fear strict judgment. Their devotion includes family and social responsibilities as well as awareness of the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: And ˹they are˺ those who endure patiently, seeking their Lord’s pleasure, establish prayer,
phrases.explanation: The believers endure patiently while seeking their Lord’s pleasure. Their patience is directed toward Allah rather than toward praise or immediate reward from people. They establish prayer as a regular act of worship. The practice keeps their relationship with Allah central through the demands of daily life.

phrases.translation: donate from what We have provided for them—secretly and openly—and respond to evil with good. It is they who will have the ultimate abode
phrases.explanation: They give from what Allah provides, both privately and publicly. Their generosity does not depend on being seen, though they may also give openly when appropriate. They answer evil with good and receive the ultimate abode. This response breaks cycles of retaliation and reflects confidence in Allah’s lasting reward.

phrases.translation: the Gardens of Eternity, which they will enter along with the righteous among their parents, spouses, and descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, ˹saying,˺
phrases.explanation: The righteous are promised the Gardens of Eternity. The name emphasizes that their home with Allah is lasting rather than a temporary comfort. They enter with righteous parents, spouses, and descendants. The promise includes the joy of family companionship where those loved ones share the same faith and good conduct. Angels enter upon them from every gate with a greeting. The scene portrays welcome and honor at the arrival in Paradise.

phrases.translation: “Peace be upon you for your perseverance. How excellent is the ultimate abode!”
phrases.explanation: The angels greet the believers with peace because of their perseverance and praise the excellent final home. Their welcome connects patience through hardship with lasting safety and joy. Their perseverance has not been wasted.

phrases.translation: And those who violate Allah’s covenant after it has been affirmed, break whatever ˹ties˺ Allah has ordered to be maintained, and spread corruption in the land—it is they who will be condemned and will have the worst abode
phrases.explanation: The verse condemns those who break Allah’s covenant after affirming it. Their failure is deliberate because they had already accepted the commitment. They also break the ties Allah ordered people to maintain. This harms relationships and disregards obligations that preserve care within the community. They spread corruption and face condemnation and the worst abode. The verse links social harm with the serious consequences of violating divine guidance.

phrases.translation: Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills. And the disbelievers become prideful of ˹the pleasures of˺ this worldly life. But the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is nothing but a fleeting enjoyment
phrases.explanation: Allah gives abundant or limited provision as He wills. Different levels of worldly wealth are not, by themselves, a reliable measure of a person’s standing with Him. Disbelievers may take pride in worldly pleasures. The verse challenges that pride by asking them to compare temporary enjoyment with what follows in the Hereafter. Compared with the Hereafter, worldly life is only fleeting enjoyment. The contrast urges people to keep temporary pleasure in perspective when making lasting choices.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “If only a sign could be sent down to him from his Lord.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, Allah leaves to stray whoever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns to Him—
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers demand a sign, and the Prophet is told that Allah guides to Himself those who turn to Him while leaving others to stray. The verse places guidance with Allah and stresses the importance of turning toward Him.

phrases.translation: those who believe and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah. Surely in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort
phrases.explanation: Believers’ hearts find comfort in remembering Allah. The verse identifies remembrance as a source of inner steadiness amid uncertainty, not merely as words repeated without attention. Remembrance brings attention back to Allah rather than letting anxiety dominate the heart.

phrases.translation: Those who believe and do good, for them will be bliss and an honourable destination.”
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do good are promised bliss and an honourable destination. The verse pairs faith with action and points to a lasting outcome beyond worldly recognition. Their honor is lasting, not limited to worldly status.

phrases.translation: And so We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ to a community, like ˹We did with˺ earlier communities, so that you may recite to them what We have revealed to you. Yet they deny the Most Compassionate. Say, “He is my Lord! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. In Him I put my trust, and to Him I turn ˹in repentance˺.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is sent to a community as messengers were sent to earlier peoples. His mission belongs to a continuing history of guidance across generations. He recites what Allah has revealed, yet the people deny the Most Compassionate. Their rejection does not change the source or truth of the message. The Prophet declares Allah his Lord, places his trust in Him, and turns to Him in repentance. The answer models devotion and reliance when the audience rejects the message.

phrases.translation: If there were a recitation that could cause mountains to move, or the earth to split, or the dead to speak,
phrases.explanation: The verse imagines a recitation capable of moving mountains, splitting the earth, or making the dead speak. It uses extraordinary signs to show how powerful revelation could be if Allah willed.

phrases.translation: ˹it would have been this Quran˺.
phrases.explanation: The Quran is presented as the recitation that would contain such power. The point is not that signs are impossible, but that every extraordinary event remains subject to Allah’s will.

phrases.translation: But all matters are by Allah’s Will. Have the believers not yet realized that had Allah willed, He could have guided all of humanity?
phrases.explanation: All matters belong to Allah’s will. The statement corrects the assumption that people can demand a sign and determine when or how Allah must provide it. The verse asks whether believers realize that Allah could have guided all humanity if He had willed. The question reminds them that guidance is within His power, not something the Prophet can impose.

phrases.translation: And disasters will continue to afflict the disbelievers or strike close to their homes for their misdeeds, until Allah’s promise comes to pass. Surely Allah never fails in His promise
phrases.explanation: Disasters continue to afflict disbelievers or strike near their homes because of their misdeeds. The warning connects wrongdoing with consequences, while leaving the precise timing to Allah. These events continue until Allah’s promise is fulfilled. The verse assures believers that delay does not mean the promise has been forgotten or abandoned. Allah never fails in His promise. The final statement grounds the warning in divine reliability rather than in human power to predict the exact moment.

phrases.translation: Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you, but I delayed the disbelievers ˹for a while˺ then seized them. And how ˹horrible˺ was My punishment
phrases.explanation: Earlier messengers were ridiculed before the Prophet. Opposition to revelation is not new, and the earlier messengers’ experience offers perspective on his own rejection. Allah delayed the disbelievers for a time and then seized them. The verse warns that patience or delay is not the same as approval, and closes by recalling the severity of punishment.

phrases.translation: Is ˹there any equal to˺ the Vigilant One Who knows what every soul commits?
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether anyone can equal the Vigilant One who knows what every soul does. Allah’s complete knowledge and oversight contrast with the limited claims people make for other gods.

phrases.translation: Yet the pagans have associated others with Allah ˹in worship˺. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Name them! Or do you ˹mean to˺ inform Him of something He does not know on the earth? Or are these ˹gods˺ just empty words?”
phrases.explanation: The pagans associate partners with Allah despite His knowledge and authority. The verse challenges this practice before inviting them to identify the beings they worship. The Prophet is told to ask them to name their partners or explain whether they are merely empty words. The questions expose how difficult it is to provide real authority for the idols.

phrases.translation: In fact, the disbelievers’ falsehood has been made so appealing to them that they have been turned away from the Path.
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers’ falsehood has been made appealing to them, turning them away from the path. The verse describes how a person can become attached to error until it seems attractive.

phrases.translation: And whoever Allah leaves to stray will be left with no guide
phrases.explanation: Whoever Allah leaves to stray has no guide. The warning emphasizes the seriousness of being turned away from guidance and the need to respond while the path is still presented.

phrases.translation: For them is punishment in this worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is truly far worse. And none can shield them from Allah
phrases.explanation: Those who reject faith face punishment in this world, but the Hereafter’s punishment is far worse. The verse places immediate consequences beside the lasting outcome. No one can shield them from Allah. The warning denies that any worldly protector can cancel the final accountability described here.

phrases.translation: The description of the Paradise promised to the righteous is that under it rivers flow; eternal is its fruit as well as its shade. That is the ˹ultimate˺ outcome for the righteous. But the outcome for the disbelievers is the Fire
phrases.explanation: Paradise is described with rivers beneath it and fruit and shade that endure. The imagery conveys abundance and lasting comfort rather than a temporary worldly pleasure. This is the ultimate outcome for those who are righteous. Their reward is presented as a secure destination after a life of faith and mindful conduct. The outcome for disbelievers is the Fire. The contrast makes clear that the two paths do not lead to the same final destination.

phrases.translation: ˹The believers among˺ those who were given the Scripture rejoice at what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺, while some ˹disbelieving˺ factions deny a portion of it. Say, “I have only been commanded to worship Allah, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺. To Him I invite ˹all˺, and to Him is my return.”
phrases.explanation: Some people given Scripture rejoice at the revelation sent to the Prophet. Their response shows that parts of the new message are recognized by people familiar with earlier revelation. Other factions deny part of the revelation. The verse acknowledges disagreement rather than pretending every group responds in the same way. The Prophet is commanded to worship Allah alone, invite people to Him, and return to Him. His mission is grounded in exclusive devotion and repentance.

phrases.translation: And so We have revealed it as an authority in Arabic.
phrases.explanation: The Quran is revealed in Arabic as an authority and guidance. The verse emphasizes both its language for its first hearers and its role in clarifying what they should follow.

phrases.translation: And if you were to follow their desires after ˹all˺ the knowledge that has come to you, there would be none to protect or shield you from Allah
phrases.explanation: If the Prophet followed the people’s desires after knowledge came, no one could protect him from Allah. The warning underscores the importance of remaining faithful to revelation even under pressure.

phrases.translation: We have certainly sent messengers before you ˹O Prophet˺ and blessed them with wives and offspring. It was not for any messenger to bring a sign without Allah’s permission. Every destined matter has a ˹set˺ time
phrases.explanation: Earlier messengers had wives and children. The verse places prophets within ordinary family life rather than treating marriage or descendants as incompatible with their mission. No messenger can bring a sign without Allah’s permission. The messenger conveys guidance but does not control miracles or set the conditions for belief. Every destined matter has a set time. The statement reminds people that events unfold according to Allah’s timing, even when they want immediate answers.

phrases.translation: Allah eliminates and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Master Record
phrases.explanation: Allah eliminates or confirms what He wills. The verse affirms His authority over what unfolds and what remains, without placing the final record in human hands. With Allah is the Master Record. The phrase points to a complete record held by Him, beyond what people can alter or fully comprehend.

phrases.translation: Whether We show you ˹O Prophet˺ some of what We threaten them with, or cause you to die ˹before that˺, your duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺. Judgment is for Us
phrases.explanation: Whether the Prophet sees some threatened events or dies before they occur, his duty is to deliver the message. The warning does not depend on him witnessing every outcome. Judgment belongs to Allah. The Prophet’s responsibility is to convey guidance, while the final decision about people’s actions rests with their Lord.

phrases.translation: Do they not see that We gradually reduce their land from its borders? Allah decides—none can reverse His decision. And He is swift in reckoning
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether people see land gradually reduced from its borders. Changing territory and power are signs that human control is not permanent. Allah decides, and no one can reverse His decision. The statement places political changes and final outcomes within His authority. Allah is swift in reckoning. People should not assume that a gradual change means accountability has been postponed forever.

phrases.translation: Those ˹disbelievers˺ before them ˹secretly˺ planned, but Allah has the ultimate plan. He knows what every soul commits. And the disbelievers will soon know who will have the ultimate outcome
phrases.explanation: Earlier disbelievers made secret plans, but Allah’s plan prevails. Human schemes may seem effective for a time, yet they cannot defeat His purpose. Allah knows what every soul does. No hidden plot or private intention is outside His knowledge. The disbelievers will soon learn who has the ultimate outcome. The verse turns their attention from temporary schemes to the final result known to Allah.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “You ˹Muḥammad˺ are no messenger.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah is sufficient as a Witness between me and you, as is whoever has knowledge of the Scripture.”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers deny that the Prophet is a messenger. Their rejection does not itself settle the question of his mission or erase the evidence already presented. The Prophet is told that Allah is sufficient as a witness, along with those who know Scripture. The verse points to divine testimony and recognition from people familiar with revelation.
